# Macro Regime

## TL;DR

**Partial risk-on recovery on May 5, but Iran tail risk unresolved.** The May 4 risk-off shock (Iran missile strikes on US warship near Jask) has partially unwound: S&P 500 and Nasdaq recovered on May 5, with Nasdaq reaching an intraday ATH. However, the Iran-UAE/Strait of Hormuz conflict has escalated further — missiles and drones targeted the UAE while Strait of Hormuz closure risk remains active, keeping oil above $102/bbl. The macro regime is best characterized as **mixed-to-cautiously-bullish**: solid earnings are providing a near-term offset, but geopolitical left-tail risk has not been removed. Hawkish Fed leadership transition on May 15 adds policy uncertainty. [source: web_research/META.json macro_context, run 20260505_140723]

## Fed posture

The Federal Reserve voted 8-4 on April 29 to hold the federal funds rate at **3.5%–3.75%** — third consecutive hold. The 4 dissents (most since Oct 1992) reflect internal disagreement. Chair Powell's last day is May 15; Kevin Warsh is the leading successor candidate (hawkish, Senate confirmation pending). Market pricing: zero cuts in 2026, one 25bp cut in December 2027. The transition introduces policy uncertainty independent of the rate level — growth stocks (META, MSFT, NVDA) are most exposed to tightening-bias tail risk. [source: web_research/META.json macro_context, run 20260505_140723]

## Rate trajectory and inflation

Inflation remains above the 2% target. Oil above $102/bbl (Brent elevated) sustains energy-driven inflation overhang. The Strait of Hormuz closure scenario — if realized — would spike energy prices, re-accelerate inflation expectations, and extend the Fed's hold/tightening timeline. U.S. midterm election uncertainty (2026) adds a further policy uncertainty layer. [source: web_research/META.json macro_context, run 20260505_140723]

## Market context (May 5)

S&P 500 and Nasdaq recovered +0.7%/+1% on May 5 with Nasdaq hitting an intraday ATH, partially reversing the May 4 sell-off (Dow -1.13%, S&P -0.41%). Solid earnings from several companies are providing the near-term offset. AI capex supercycle narrative is challenged at the margin (META -9% capex shock, MSFT post-earnings selloff) but Alphabet/Amazon cloud beats and Azure +40% keep the thesis alive. Snap Q1 2026 earnings due ~May 6 — digital ad market health read-through. [source: web_research/META.json macro_context, run 20260505_140723]

## Geopolitical and regulatory

**Iran-UAE conflict is the dominant risk.** Iran launched missiles and drones at the UAE and targeted a ship in the Strait of Hormuz after a brief ceasefire expired. Strait of Hormuz closure threat (global oil supply choke point) is a live left-tail scenario. Additional flashpoints: US-Venezuela tensions, NATO posture in Greenland, residual tariff uncertainty. Fed leadership transition (May 15) is the most proximate policy risk. [source: web_research/META.json macro_context, run 20260505_140723]

## Risk-off triggers

- **Iran-Strait of Hormuz escalation** — closure or prolonged blockade spikes oil, re-accelerates inflation
- **Kevin Warsh hawkish confirmation signal** — tighter-for-longer signals growth stocks re-rate lower
- **AI capex ROI disappointment** — any major AI infrastructure player signaling wasted spend
- **US tariff escalation** — additional rounds pressure supply chains and consumer sentiment
- **US midterm election volatility** — policy uncertainty ahead of 2026 midterms

Supersedes prior entry (2026-05-04, run 20260504_125732) which reflected pure risk-off mood from the Iran missile strike — May 5 partial recovery and UAE/Strait of Hormuz escalation update warrant a full rewrite.

thesis_tldr.content:
**Prior thesis falsified.** The bootstrap thesis described UNH as a "beaten-down healthcare giant down 54% from all-time highs" with a contrarian recovery setup. That framing is now obsolete: Q1 2026 earnings (April 21) crushed estimates ($7.23 adj. EPS vs $6.57 est.) and the stock surged +41.6% in 21 trading days to $370.74. UNH is no longer a recovery play — it is an extended momentum leader at statistical extremes (RSI 94.3, z-score 2.54, ADX 81.64). The correct posture is wait for a pullback to the $348–355 EMA zone before re-entering long. (Source: decisions.json, explanation.json, web_research/UNH.json, run 20260430_194522.)

**What falsified the prior thesis:** The April 21 Q1 2026 earnings beat — adj. EPS $7.23 vs $6.57 consensus, revenue $111.72B vs $109.57B, medical cost ratio improved to 84%, full-year guidance raised to >$18.25 — confirmed the recovery thesis was correct in direction but rendered the "discounted valuation" framing stale. Price is now extended, not discounted. (Source: web_research/UNH.json, run 20260430_194522.)
